cards.lore: Every party needs the one who read none of the rulebook and still showed up on time.
cards.power: You pick the class with no spells and no gimmick. You hit things with a sword.

cards.lore: The fighter's superpower is not dying when everyone had already written him off.
cards.power: You catch your breath mid-fight. You are somehow still standing.

cards.lore: While the casters debated the lore, the fighter solved the problem. Twice.
cards.power: You take two turns in one. Nobody questions how.

cards.lore: The class with no story is the one the story could not happen without.
cards.power: You did the most damage all campaign. No one noticed.

cards.lore: Every barbarian's first session begins with a door that did not need breaking.
cards.power: You rage. You go in first. You ask questions never.

cards.lore: The barbarian found the button that makes the numbers bigger. The barbarian presses the button.
cards.power: You trade your defense for damage. You consider this a good deal.

cards.lore: A hero who solves problems by hitting them will be handed every problem.
cards.power: The party sends you into every room first. You believe this is honor.

cards.lore: At high enough level, the barbarian stops being a character and beco[m—text clipped at page edge]
cards.power: You rage again. There was no cooldown anyway.

cards.lore: The wizard begins as the smartest person in the room and the easiest to kill.
cards.power: You throw a tiny magic dart. You have four hit points.

cards.lore: A wizard's power is infinite, in theory, once per day.
cards.power: You have the perfect spell for this. You used it last encounter.

cards.lore: Knowing exactly how the world works is not the same as surviving it.
cards.power: You correct the DM on the lore. You are right. It does not help.

cards.lore: At high level the wizard is a god, between naps.
cards.power: You end the encounter in one spell. You also end yourself in one hit.

cards.lore: The wizard earned it. The sorcerer woke up with it and never let the wizard forget.
cards.power: You did magic. You don't know how. You did not study.

cards.lore: Innate power comes with innate consequences and no instruction manual.
cards.power: You cast a spell. The DM rolls on a table. Everyone holds their breath.

cards.lore: Talent is the only thing more annoying than the person who has it.
cards.power: You out-cast the wizard while eating. The wizard files a complaint.

cards.lore: Raw power never asked permission and never reads the room.
cards.power: You reshape the spell mid-cast. It might fireball the party.

cards.lore: Nobody chooses to be the medic. The party chooses for them.
cards.power: You wanted to fight. The party voted you the healer.

cards.lore: A healer learns whom to save by who screams the most convincingly.
cards.power: You heal the loudest first. Volume is not the same as injury.

cards.lore: Divine mercy comes with a free divine opinion.
cards.power: You heal the rogue. You make sure the rogue knows how you feel about it.

cards.lore: Everyone forgets the cleric exists until the exact moment they need her.
cards.power: You are out of spells. The party turns to you anyway.

cards.lore: The druid knows the forest intimately and trusts it completely, which is the problem.
cards.power: You identify every plant. You eat the wrong one anyway.

cards.lore: Give a druid one animal form and every encounter becomes that animal.
cards.power: You turn into a bear. You will be solving most problems as a bear now.

cards.lore: No one invited the lecture. The lecture comes free with the nature magic.
cards.power: You stop the raid to explain why the dungeon is unsustainable.

cards.lore: A druid who can be anything will, eventually, just be the bear.
cards.power: You have not been a person in three sessions. The party has stopped asking.

cards.lore: The rogue's first level is mostly the party standing in a hallway.
cards.power: You check every door, chest, and floor tile for traps. The party waits.

cards.lore: The rogue does nothing for five rounds and then settles the whole fight.
cards.power: You stab it once for damage the fighter dreams about.

cards.lore: A rogue does not distinguish between enemy pockets and friendly ones.
cards.power: You loot the body before the party reaches it. You looted the party too.

cards.cardName: The I Was Never Here Rogue
cards.lore: The perfect heist leaves no evidence, only a confused bard.
cards.power: You vanish before the consequences arrive. The blame lands on the bard.

cards.lore: The ranger sees a story in the mud that no one asked him to narrate.
cards.power: You read the trail. You know what passed, when, and how it felt about it.

cards.lore: A ranger prepares perfectly for the one enemy he will never meet.
cards.power: You chose goblins as your sworn nemesis at character creation.

cards.lore: The wilderness expert becomes furniture the moment there is a roof.
cards.power: You have no idea how to talk to a shopkeeper. You offer to track him instead.

cards.lore: The ranger spent four levels becoming the second most interesting member of his own duo.
cards.power: Your animal companion does the cool thing. Everyone pets the wolf. Not you.

cards.lore: Every bard's career begins with an audience that did not consent.
cards.power: You perform for the tavern. Some of them even wanted you to.

cards.lore: The bard's true magic is making other people slightly more confident than they should be.
cards.power: You tell the fighter he's doing great. The fighter rolls better. Science cannot explain it.

cards.lore: The bard has never met a plot he could not complicate with flirtation.
cards.power: You attempt to romance the quest-giver, the villain, and the dragon. In that order.

cards.lore: History is written by the bard, which is why the bard always wins it.
cards.power: You write the ballad of the campaign. You are the hero of every verse.

cards.lore: The paladin's oath is the most sincere thing at a table built on lying to a DM.
cards.power: You take the oath. You mean every word with your whole heart.

cards.lore: The paladin saves it all up for one righteous moment and spends it loudly.
cards.power: You pour every spell slot into one holy hit. The undead simply leaves.

cards.lore: Every party gets the conscience it deserves and none of them wanted.
cards.power: You remind the party that stealing is wrong. The party was mid-steal.

cards.lore: The longer the oath holds, the more creative the holding becomes.
cards.power: You found a loophole in your own oath. You are still good. Mostly.

cards.lore: The monk arrives at the dungeon dressed for a completely different occasion.
cards.power: You have no armor and no weapon. You have a philosophy and bad feet.

cards.lore: Nobody respected the punching class until the punching started.
cards.power: You punch four times in the time it takes the fighter to swing once.

cards.lore: The monk spends the whole campaign being a surprise to people who read his sheet.
cards.power: You deflect the arrow, walk on the water, and say something cryptic.

cards.lore: At high level there is no problem the monk cannot solve by hitting it with his hands specifically.
cards.power: You punch the dragon. The dragon was not built for this matchup.

cards.lore: The warlock got everything everything he wanted and one clause he did not read.
cards.power: You sign the deal for power. You skim the terms.

cards.lore: Give a warlock one good attack and he will never learn another.
cards.power: You fire the same beam again. You will fire it every turn forever.

cards.lore: Power on loan comes with a landlord who visits without warning.
cards.power: Your patron whispers a side-quest mid-dungeon. You cannot say no.

cards.lore: Every warlock learns the same lesson on the last page of the contract.
cards.power: Your patron arrives to collect. You are now part of the dungeon.

cards.lore: The necromancer's hobby is everyone else's nightmare and he cannot understand why.
cards.power: You loot the cemetery for parts. You call it research.

cards.lore: A necromancer's first creation is the first friend who could not leave.
cards.power: You raise your first skeleton. You named it. You are attached now.

cards.lore: The necromancer is the only class whose party-balance problem is social.
cards.power: You bring your skeletons to the tavern. The party sits at the other table.

cards.lore: A man who builds his own company has only the company he built.
cards.power: You command two hundred undead. You have never been more alone.

cards.lore: Every DM begins by mistaking the module for the campaign.
cards.power: You write forty pages of lore. The players will read none of it.

cards.lore: A DM's real skill is named "yes, and" and learned the hard way.
cards.power: The players go left. Everything you prepared was to the right. You smile and invent a town.

cards.lore: The hardest roll a DM makes is the one against his own outline.
cards.power: You feel the urge to force the plot. You resist. Mostly.

cards.lore: Stay fluffy.
cards.power: You set the table. The players arrive. You do not pretend to know what happens next.

title: Plato's Dungeon Raid — Full Class Roster v05
